subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: Should iMessage drop non-group, not-from-me DMs before access control when sender normalizes to destination_caller_id and no canonical peer can be recovered, or should this PR only repair confident peer candidates?
rationale: The repaired sender becomes the authorization subject, pairing id, session route, and reply target, so the fallback policy is a real identity-boundary choice rather than a purely mechanical refactor.

options.title: Require Canonical Repair Or Drop
options.body: Use canonical iMessage normalization for all candidate comparisons and fail closed when the peer cannot be recovered confidently before access control.

options.title: Repair Confident Candidates Only
options.body: Limit the PR to canonical peer recovery and leave unrepairable local-sender rows to the existing downstream behavior until a separate policy decision lands.

options.title: Pause Until Root Cause Is Clear
options.body: Keep the branch open but paused if the author's remaining failures indicate a different iMessage sender or pairing root cause.

recommendation.title: Require Canonical Repair Or Drop
recommendation.body: Use canonical iMessage normalization for all candidate comparisons and fail closed when the peer cannot be recovered confidently before access control.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent destination_caller_id self-chat work is the closest merged history for this identity boundary.
